title: Honest Interval Length for Rank Interaction under a Union Null in Factorial Experiments
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; paper_score_ceiling=6.8 < 7.4. Math panel PASS; independent boundary consult confirms no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: The delivered proofs establish the same-class worst-null expected-length rate min{1,M^(3/8)/sqrt(n)}, including full-parent coverage and an original-record all-interval converse; unknown-profile adaptation is not a load-bearing gap. The profile results provide brackets and selected matching regimes, not a general characterization of H_rho or the adaptation loss. The contribution resides in branch normalization, the rank-functional modulus and the constrained converse, rather than the polynomial collision machinery already supplied by [CDKS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11560). Its causal applicability requires shared ranks, uniform public contexts, fair independent factors and independent respondents, so it cannot certify the clustered intervals in [Zhang–Gao](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v323/zhang26a.html). The primary attaining interval is deterministically [0,1] for every n <= 36,286,141,440 because T >= 80B/n; the additional profile certificate supplies special-regime improvements but no demonstrated practical worst-null calibration, which limits the projected paper score alongside the specialized model. The TL;DR and Honest scope retain stale target/deferred-proof language despite the supplied proofs, but neither asserts that the open profile-adaptation problem has been solved. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed the complete-null honest-length rate min(1, M^(3/8)/sqrt(n)), an observable full-parent interval and an original-record all-interval converse, plus a partial profile envelope. Mathematical review and an independent boundary consult found no false headline or laundering, but the cold referee capped the specialized package at subfield (score ceiling 6.8 below 7.4); large conservative constants and unresolved general profile adaptation limit its reach. Formalization was not entered; removing the remaining unconsumed comparator ballast cannot raise the tier, and broader profile/adaptation work remains a separate research program.
tldr: A small factorial contrast of mean responses need not certify a small individual rank interaction. With a public uniform context menu, independent fair binary factors and one factual response per independent respondent, the complete rank-interaction null is a contextwise union of two unknown single-factor branches. The focal theorem target is a total interval with exact finite-sample coverage over the full bounded response cube and matching complete-null expected length \(\min\{1,M^{3/8}/\sqrt n\}\) at every menu size. Its load-bearing steps combine branch-normalized original-record collisions with the singular rank modulus and a permanent-table converse. Honest adaptation to unknown null branch strengths is the first-class open question. Common-rank identification, polynomial CI methods and moment matching are credited.
gap: Published causal explainability inference and discrete CI testing do not state the complete-null expected-length frontier for this fixed public-margin binary rank target.
fill: A branch-normalized whole-parent variance inequality and a nonsmooth global modulus are paired with an unconditional finite-record confidence envelope. A legal permanent null prior supplies the matching all-interval lower and the menu/sample frontier.
